about.title: About
about.goalText:
To be free. A bike, a tent and a few spare inner tubes…

The goal — you need one as a pretext to leave — my wheels will start turning in Alaska, far north at Prudhoe Bay, inside the Arctic Circle.

The destination? I don't know yet — that is the beauty of travel and adventure. The bearing is, however, set due south, to Ushuaia — some 25,000 km away in Patagonia.
about.vincentText1: Drawn to discovery, simplicity and adventure. In search of that feeling of freedom — owing nothing to anyone, pitching the tent on a whim, breathing fresh air under a deep blue starry sky or simply listening to the rain tap on the canvas, cosy and restless inside my tent.
about.vincentText2: I grew up through family bike trips, and it was through those experiences that I told myself that one day I too would do what those people do — the ones who carry their home on two wheels, unfold a map at a street corner, drink coffee along a river, ride through the rain and light up at the sight of little things: the essentials.
about.vincentText3: During a winter bivouac, head tilted back and lost in the immensity of the sky, reflecting on my future motivations, I came home with a few words written in black and white in my precious notebook: Never have regrets.
about.vincentText4: That is now the phrase that guides some of my choices when doubt, fear or uncertainty looms — and that should push us to simply DARE.
about.sponsorsText: This journey is funded by my own savings, set aside over the years. I am fortunate to have the precious material support of the partners below, big or small! If you wish to support the adventure or have your brand travel with me, feel free to get in touch.
about.coffeeText: A coffee lover and enthusiast — coffee means encounters, exchanges and laughter, and it also motivates me to keep moving and discover roads less travelled. If you'd like to give me a little wink and share an air-presso (air-espresso, def.: "performing an invisible or remote action") pinky raised, you can make a donation.
about.guideIntro: This map follows Vincent's journey from Deadhorse, Alaska to Ushuaia, Argentina. Here is what you can see, where the data comes from and how to read it.
about.guideSectionMapRides: Orange traces — rides recorded by Vincent. Click a trace to open the detail panel: distance, elevation gain, maximum altitude, top speed, breaks longer than 10 minutes, and the ride journal if he wrote one. If the activity has Strava comments, a speech bubble icon appears next to the date — click it to read them. The title and description come from the Strava activity by default; Vincent can edit them manually but does not always have the time or energy to do so.
about.guideSectionMapRoute: Dashed cyan line — the planned itinerary from Deadhorse to Ushuaia. It serves as a reference to measure progress.
about.guideSectionMapPhotos: Photo markers — geotagged photos from Vincent's Strava activities and his Flickr account. Only photos with GPS coordinates appear on the map. Click to enlarge.
about.guideSectionMediaText: The Media tab gathers all photos and videos in a three-column grid, sorted newest first. Click any thumbnail to view it fullscreen. In fullscreen mode, use the left/right arrows (or keyboard arrow keys) to browse. Press Escape to close.
about.guideSectionMapWeather: Weather layer — current conditions sampled roughly every 50 km along the planned route: temperature, humidity, wind direction and animated speed. Only visible from a zoom level equivalent to viewing a large country (around level 7). Data is refreshed every day at 06:00 UTC. Enable it from the Geo tools panel.
about.guideSectionMapCities: City markers (?) — major towns near the route, visible from a regional zoom level (level 9, roughly the size of a province). Relief markers — notable mountains, passes and lakes along the route, visible from a country-level zoom (level 7). Click any marker to read a Wikipedia summary in your language.
about.guideSectionMapBasemap: Base map — accessible from the Geo tools panel (top-left button). Switch between the default dark style and the topo view. The choice is not remembered between sessions.
about.guideSectionMapPosition: Pulsing cyan dot — Vincent's position on the map corresponds to the end point of his last recorded Strava activity.
about.guideSectionGeoToolsRouteProfil: Route profile — shows the elevation profile of the planned route (Deadhorse → Ushuaia). Click directly on the dashed cyan line on the map, or enable it from this panel. Hover the chart to see Vincent's progress in real time.
about.guideSectionGeoToolsMeasure: Measure distance — click points on the map to draw a geodesic (great-circle) line and read the total distance. Double-click to finish, Escape to cancel.
about.guideSectionGeoToolsTrueSize: True size (CH) — overlays Switzerland at its real geographic scale so you can compare it to any region Vincent is crossing. Drag it anywhere on the map.
about.guideSectionGeoToolsTimezone: Time zones — colours the world map by UTC offset. Hover a zone to see the current local time, corrected for daylight saving.
about.guideSectionGeoToolsDaylight: Daylight — draws the current solar terminator line with a faint day/night overlay, calculated in real time from the sun's position.
about.guideSectionGeoToolsPopDensity: Population density — overlays the EU Copernicus GHS-POP 2025 layer showing the number of inhabitants per 100 × 100 m cell. Available at all zoom levels. Use the opacity slider to adjust the intensity. The built-in legend shows the colour scale: from pale purple (0–5 inhabitants) to dark burgundy (1 000+).
about.guideSectionGeoToolsFires: Active fires (24 h) — overlays thermal anomalies detected by the MODIS satellites (Terra + Aqua) over the past 24 hours, via NASA's GIBS service. Each point represents a fire or intense heat detection on the ground. Data has a 2–3 day processing lag.
about.guideSectionGeoToolsWildlife: Wildlife (Faune & Flore) — queries the GBIF global biodiversity database for species observations around the visible area. Only available at zoom level 9 or above. Filter by group (birds, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, insects, plants), radius (25 / 50 / 100 km), observation period, month, and photo availability. Circular markers are animals; diamond markers are plants. Click a marker to see the species name, photo, and observation date. Click the photo to enlarge it.
about.guideSectionDataTitle: Where does the data come from?
about.guideSectionDataStrava: Rides and photos: imported automatically from Strava, Vincent's activity tracking app. He must publish activities manually from his phone; depending on field conditions (connectivity, fatigue, available time) there can be a lag of several days. Do not worry if the map does not move for a few days — it is completely normal.
about.guideSectionDataFlickr: Additional photos: from his Flickr account, for photos taken outside Strava with GPS coordinates.
about.guideSectionDataYoutube: Videos: imported from his YouTube channel.
about.guideSectionDataWeather: Weather: via the Open-Meteo API, refreshed every day at 06:00 UTC.
about.guideSectionDataWiki: City and point-of-interest descriptions: fetched on demand from Wikipedia, in your language when available, otherwise in English.
about.guideSectionDataPopDensity: Population density: GHS-POP 2025 layer from the EU Copernicus programme, 100 × 100 m resolution.
about.guideSectionDataLightning: Live lightning: Blitzortung.org community detection network, data refreshed in real time via WebSocket.
about.guideSectionDataFires: Active fires: thermal anomalies from Terra and Aqua satellites (MODIS), served via NASA's GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services) portal. Data is available with a 2–3 day lag.
about.guideSectionDataGbif: Wildlife observations: queried live from the GBIF Global Biodiversity Information Facility database. Data is not stored — every activation fetches fresh results directly from their API.
about.guideSectionFreshnessTitle: How up to date is the data?
about.guideSectionFreshnessText: All data (rides, photos, videos, weather) is synchronised once a day at 06:00 UTC. Vincent's progress depends on his ability to publish Strava activities from the field. Several days may pass without an update — this is normal and does not mean the journey has stopped.
about.guideSectionHomeScreenText: The map works well on mobile. You can add a shortcut to your home screen to open it in one tap, without going through a browser — handy for checking Vincent's progress day to day. This creates a shortcut to the website, not a downloaded app.
about.guideSectionHomeScreenIos: iPhone — Open this page in Safari, tap the Share button, then "Add to Home Screen".
about.guideSectionHomeScreenAndroid: Android — Open this page in Chrome, tap the menu (three dots), then "Add to Home Screen".
about.guideSectionSuggestText: Have an idea to improve the map or the site? Send us a message.
about.changelogV10desc: Bootstrap Next.js, Supabase schema, Strava sync (OAuth + polylines + cron) and Flickr (GPS photos), Leaflet map with trips and photos, individual trip detail pages, admin panel (login, trip management, content editor), FR/EN bilingual.
about.changelogV11desc: Interactive elevation profile with hover sync, Open-Meteo weather layer along planned route, Alaska-Ushuaia planned route overlay, Strava activity photos synced to map, full mobile redesign (bottom sheet panel), stats (elevation gain, countries crossed), OrbiTerra rebrand, crons merged into single daily job.
about.changelogV12desc: Max speed, max altitude and break callout markers with leader lines on map. Animated globe on landing page, Vincent live position marker. Cities and POIs (mountains, passes, lakes) with Wikipedia panels (200+ entries). YouTube video of the day per trip (automatic date matching) with hover preview and fullscreen modal. Charmey Sports and Molechaux sponsors. 3-line expandable journal.
about.changelogV13desc: Media tab (photo+video gallery with lightbox, /api/gallery endpoint). Vincent's text in About, coffee donation link. New landing page composition, bicycle favicon. Polar circles, sunrise/sunset clock. Bike setup tab (Fairlight + full kit with links). Geo tools: draggable Switzerland true-size overlay, distance measure, timezone layer, animated day/night overlay. Strava comments sync (last 30 days) shown in trip side panel.
about.changelogPascaleDesc: StatHunter modal with per-trip stats (speed, elevation, distance). Mobile carousel in About modal. Strava description sync to trip journal. Tent, saddle and lighting in bike setup tab. Lusty sponsor.
about.changelogV153desc: Position marker now shows the last recorded GPS point. Rider name editable from admin. Break threshold raised to 30 minutes. Strava video detection.
about.changelogV155desc: Added boat and plane transfers on the map, rendered as great-circle arcs between two points.
